title: DWP demonstration learning programme
introduction: Choose a role and learning objective. Completion ticks record activity, not assessed competence. This is a draft curriculum awaiting lesson publication.

paths.title: Read evidence before trusting an answer
paths.description: Build a reproducible claim-to-evidence ledger and stop when the supplied material is insufficient.

steps.title: Baseline and role
steps.outcome: State what success looks like for your role.
steps.practice: Answer three baseline prompts without help; retain them for later comparison.

steps.title: Distinguish the layers
steps.outcome: Separate original guidance, extracted text and project-authored interpretation.
steps.practice: Classify three items and explain the authority each does and does not have.

steps.title: Read the source in context
steps.outcome: Check a paragraph with its heading and continuation.
steps.practice: Capture the locator and a qualification that would be lost in an isolated quotation.

steps.title: Use concepts without overclaiming
steps.outcome: Distinguish a mention tag, semantic assertion and legal applicability.
steps.practice: Explain why each visible link is or is not enough to support a claim.

steps.title: Separate search, context and answer
steps.outcome: Identify which operation finds records, assembles evidence or generates an answer.
steps.practice: Draw the three stages and name the artefact returned by each.

steps.title: Read insufficiency honestly
steps.outcome: Distinguish retained candidates, required evidence and unresolved obligations.
steps.practice: Write three separately defined denominators and identify an omitted requirement.

steps.title: Make the result accessible
steps.outcome: Explain a result without relying on colour, jargon or pointer-only actions.
steps.practice: Use keyboard navigation and give a plain-English explanation with one source and one gap.

steps.title: Foundation assessment
steps.outcome: Apply the evidence rubric independently.
steps.practice: Submit a claim ledger, a refused unsupported conclusion and a reproducible source identity.

paths.title: Absence abroad and residence
paths.description: Scope absence questions and expose benefit-specific exceptions without making a universal claim.

steps.title: Set the scope
steps.outcome: Name the missing benefit, jurisdiction, dates and purpose.
steps.practice: Write the minimum clarification questions.

steps.title: Scope a journey abroad
steps.outcome: Distinguish the benefit, destination, duration, purpose and relevant period before selecting evidence.
steps.practice: Create a clarification tree; compare temporary absence, treatment and permanent departure without claiming one universal rule.

steps.title: Inspect territorial assumptions
steps.outcome: Locate the territorial and temporal scope of a candidate passage.
steps.practice: Annotate what cannot be carried into another jurisdiction.

steps.title: Pension Credit and a move abroad
steps.outcome: Re-scope the general absence question for the named benefit and temporary/permanent distinction.
steps.practice: Create a benefit-specific evidence plan and explain why the general absence result cannot simply be copied.

steps.title: Read continuations
steps.outcome: Avoid treating the first matching paragraph as the whole rule.
steps.practice: Follow the chapter context and record a remaining source dependency.

steps.title: Change a material fact
steps.outcome: Explain why a permanent move cannot inherit a temporary-absence conclusion.
steps.practice: Submit a before/after evidence-requirement table.

steps.title: Absence assessment
steps.outcome: Give a qualified evidence plan for an unseen absence scenario.
steps.practice: Submit scope, sources, exceptions and an escalation decision.

paths.title: Pension regimes, age and transitions
paths.description: Separate age, regime, conditions, claim and payment across State Pension and disability transitions.

steps.title: Create a regime map
steps.outcome: Separate new State Pension from the legacy regime.
steps.practice: Draw two source branches and list the date needed to choose between them.

steps.title: Separate age from first entitlement
steps.outcome: Distinguish pensionable age, qualifying conditions, claim and payment dates.
steps.practice: For the supplied birth-date example, mark which date questions the captured table can support and which need further evidence; do not produce an entitlement decision.

steps.title: Separate pension regimes and components
steps.outcome: Identify new State Pension, legacy retirement pension and transitional evidence as different scopes.
steps.practice: Produce a regime-and-component map with source-backed prerequisites and an unresolved NI-record boundary.

steps.title: IIDB around pension age
steps.outcome: Distinguish IIDB from Reduced Earnings Allowance and related age-dependent questions.
steps.practice: Create a transition table with independent evidence requirements for each named benefit.

steps.title: PIP around pension age
steps.outcome: Distinguish the treatment of an existing award from a new claim at a different date.
steps.practice: Submit a change-of-facts counterexample and the evidence it requires.

steps.title: Audit the age table
steps.outcome: Preserve the table heading, band and continuation.
steps.practice: Explain what the table establishes and what it does not establish.

steps.title: Remove the date
steps.outcome: Recognise when an answer becomes unsupported after a date or regime is removed.
steps.practice: Reject or qualify a deliberately under-specified synthetic case.

steps.title: Transition assessment
steps.outcome: Present a regime-aware evidence brief.
steps.practice: Submit a timeline separating qualification, claim, award and payment.

paths.title: Pension Credit inputs and calculation structure
paths.description: Explain Pension Credit assessment dependencies without turning incomplete guidance into an award calculator.

steps.title: Distinguish the decisions
steps.outcome: Separate eligibility, inputs, components and payable amount.
steps.practice: Sketch four boxes and the evidence each requires.

steps.title: Explain Pension Credit clearly
steps.outcome: Give a plain-English structural explanation while separating source statements from interpretation.
steps.practice: Write a short explanation and an evidence ledger; retain limitations instead of hiding them in a footnote.

steps.title: Trace qualification conditions
steps.outcome: Separate demonstrated conditions from assumptions about facts, dates and regime.
steps.practice: Create a conditions-and-evidence checklist with an explicit cannot-determine outcome.

steps.title: Challenge the savings-maximum premise
steps.outcome: Distinguish capital, valuation, disregards and income treatment from a single assumed cut-off.
steps.practice: Create a dependency map; label missing conditions rather than returning a universal savings maximum.

steps.title: Map assessment elements
steps.outcome: Separate an input, an eligibility condition and a calculation parameter.
steps.practice: Classify every proposed threshold and identify the source, period and unresolved dependency.

steps.title: Specify calculation inputs
steps.outcome: Trace proposed inputs to their purpose, evidence and applicability.
steps.practice: Produce an input dictionary that separates unknown, zero, not applicable and not supplied.

steps.title: Describe calculation dependencies
steps.outcome: Represent the structure of a calculation without treating an incomplete source package as an executable formula.
steps.practice: Draw a dependency graph with units, effective periods and unresolved branches; do not calculate an award.

steps.title: Separate eligibility from rate
steps.outcome: Keep the qualifying test, component and dated rate as distinct evidence needs.
steps.practice: Prepare a review brief that cannot collapse these three decisions into one lookup.

steps.title: Test a misleading threshold
steps.outcome: Detect a capital example being presented as a universal maximum.
steps.practice: Repair the claim and show the missing valuation or disregard dependency.

steps.title: Calculation-structure assessment
steps.outcome: Explain a complete design with explicit unresolved branches.
steps.practice: Submit the dependency graph and input dictionary; no personal award or production formula.

paths.title: Historical rates, additions and ambiguous terms
paths.description: Construct a date-bound evidence series and resolve SDA without inventing missing values.

steps.title: Define the five-period window
steps.outcome: Turn a relative request into an explicit reproducible period.
steps.practice: Record the as-of date and agree five benefit years; for the demo use 2022/23–2026/27 as a proposed window, subject to available evidence.

steps.title: Resolve SDA before retrieving rates
steps.outcome: Keep Severe Disablement Allowance distinct from the Pension Credit severe-disability addition.
steps.practice: Ask for clarification and build two separately labelled evidence routes; do not choose a meaning silently.

steps.title: Build a dated Pension Credit series
steps.outcome: Bind each rate observation to an effective period, component and source version.
steps.practice: Populate a five-period evidence table; explicitly leave unavailable observations blank.

steps.title: Additional amounts over time
steps.outcome: Distinguish separate additional amounts and their qualifying conditions in a dated comparison.
steps.practice: Create a component-by-period matrix; record both missing rates and missing qualifications.

steps.title: Separate effective and capture dates
steps.outcome: Identify which date governs a rate observation.
steps.practice: Label a source date, effective period and acquisition date separately.

steps.title: Keep missing observations missing
steps.outcome: Avoid filling an absent year from memory or interpolation.
steps.practice: Add a gap row and a source acquisition requirement.

steps.title: Test a mislabelled amount
steps.outcome: Detect an amount assigned to the wrong component or period.
steps.practice: Correct a deliberately relabelled table cell and explain the evidence.

steps.title: Rates assessment
steps.outcome: Produce an auditable historical comparison.
steps.practice: Submit the table, terminology decision, gaps and provenance; never substitute a present rate.

paths.title: Partners, household and care-home changes
paths.description: Preserve household qualifications and distinguish permanence, funding and components when reviewing care-home questions.

steps.title: Model the facts
steps.outcome: Distinguish partner status, household membership, permanence and funding.
steps.practice: Create a synthetic fact matrix without claimant identifiers.

steps.title: Identify relevant partner facts
steps.outcome: Distinguish partner, couple, household membership and a person merely sharing accommodation.
steps.practice: Build a fact-to-definition table and flag any missing facts before proposing an interpretation.

steps.title: Test the partner comparison
steps.outcome: Explain how a partner scenario changes the evidence needed rather than just changing a numeric amount.
steps.practice: Compare synthetic single and couple fact patterns while keeping all other facts constant.

steps.title: Self-funded permanent care
steps.outcome: Retain partner and household qualifications while examining a self-funded scenario.
steps.practice: Write a qualified evidence note with headings, continuations and household assumptions visible.

steps.title: Publicly funded permanent care
steps.outcome: Show why changing funding does not remove the need to check household and component rules.
steps.practice: Compare with the self-funded scenario; annotate every changed fact and unresolved dependency.

steps.title: Challenge all care-home scenarios
steps.outcome: Define a bounded scenario space and identify what an all-scenarios claim would require.
steps.practice: Submit a matrix of permanence, funding, partner/household and component distinctions, with uncovered cells.

steps.title: Read the qualifying heading
steps.outcome: Detect a source heading that limits a quoted proposition.
steps.practice: Annotate the heading and continuation before accepting a claim.

steps.title: Check ignored-person dependencies
steps.outcome: Recognise why sharing accommodation alone may not settle a disability-addition question.
steps.practice: Record normal-residence, ignored-person and partner dependencies still needing review.

steps.title: Review a plausible AI answer
steps.outcome: Find a material omission despite an exact quotation.
steps.practice: Mark the unsupported inference and rewrite it with the missing condition visible.

steps.title: Household assessment
steps.outcome: Explain changed evidence needs after a material fact changes.
steps.practice: Submit the scenario matrix and an independent critique of a new answer.

paths.title: Directed benefit interactions and disability transitions
paths.description: Distinguish qualification, income treatment, overlap, passporting and transition for named benefit variants.

steps.title: Classify an interaction
steps.outcome: Name the relation before evaluating whether it is supported.
steps.practice: Define five relation types in plain English and give a non-example of each.

steps.title: Draw directed edges
steps.outcome: Keep source, target, component and regime explicit.
steps.practice: Demonstrate why an A-to-B relation cannot simply be reversed.

steps.title: State Pension and PIP
steps.outcome: Distinguish separate qualification from an assumed payment offset.
steps.practice: Draw a directed interaction with explicit component, period and unresolved evidence.

steps.title: Other benefits alongside State Pension
steps.outcome: Separate possible additional support from established entitlement.
steps.practice: Make a candidate-benefit matrix with a qualifying-condition column; reject automatic passporting.

steps.title: Housing Benefit and Pension Credit
steps.outcome: Distinguish income treatment, housing costs and passporting direction.
steps.practice: Draw separate candidate relationships and identify what evidence is needed for each.

steps.title: State Pension within Pension Credit research
steps.outcome: Distinguish receipt of one benefit from qualification for another and the treatment of income.
steps.practice: Prepare a directed interaction note with an explicit counterexample to automatic entitlement.

steps.title: Additional support with IIDB
steps.outcome: Separate IIDB qualification, supplements and other benefit conditions.
steps.practice: Build a candidate-support map; mark every unproven dependency.

steps.title: Child DLA to PIP: first occurrence
steps.outcome: Distinguish age-related transition, an existing award, a new claim and relevant dates.
steps.practice: Capture the exact governed input tuple and an unresolved transition checklist for later replay.

steps.title: IIDB and JSA variants
steps.outcome: Separate income-based, contributory and New Style JSA before discussing interactions.
steps.practice: Compare three variant-specific evidence plans; reject a single unqualified yes/no answer.

steps.title: IIDB and ESA variants
steps.outcome: Separate income-related, contributory and New Style ESA before discussing interactions.
steps.practice: Build a variant matrix that identifies missing overlap and income-treatment evidence.

steps.title: IIDB and disability benefit families
steps.outcome: Distinguish benefit-level associations from component-specific payment rules.
steps.practice: Make a directed component map for IIDB, PIP, Attendance Allowance and DLA with provenance.

steps.title: IIDB and PIP in detail
steps.outcome: Explain why a related-benefit link does not prove the rule for concurrent payment.
steps.practice: Audit one candidate relationship against its cited source and list unresolved qualifications.

steps.title: Additional support associated with PIP
steps.outcome: Separate a possible qualifying benefit from automatic entitlement to a supplement.
steps.practice: Prepare a conditions-first discovery matrix with daily-living and mobility components distinguished.

steps.title: Child DLA to PIP: replay occurrence
steps.outcome: Recognise the duplicate wording and reproduce governed evidence under identical inputs.
steps.practice: Replay staff-026 with the same version and budget; compare evidence identity, not merely answer wording.

steps.title: PIP and JSA variants
steps.outcome: Separate the PIP component from the JSA regime and proposed interaction.
steps.practice: Submit a variant-specific directed map and a negative control changing the JSA regime.

steps.title: PIP and ESA variants
steps.outcome: Separate the PIP component from the ESA regime and proposed interaction.
steps.practice: Show which evidence is shared and which must be re-established after an ESA-variant change.

steps.title: PIP, Attendance Allowance and DLA
steps.outcome: Distinguish age, component, transition and overlap questions.
steps.practice: Produce a comparison with no assumed symmetric equivalence between these benefits.

steps.title: War pensions and constant attendance
steps.outcome: Keep War Pensions Constant Attendance Allowance separate from the industrial injuries allowance.
steps.practice: Resolve the terminology, scope the requested variations and record missing rates or overlap rules instead of adding payments.

steps.title: Counterexample round
steps.outcome: Detect a variant swap and an invalid symmetric inference.
steps.practice: Correct both errors and identify the evidence to reacquire.

steps.title: Interaction assessment
steps.outcome: Produce a bounded directed interaction map.
steps.practice: Submit two variant-specific maps, duplicate-replay identities and unresolved conditions.

paths.title: Caring conditions and effects on others
paths.description: Separate caring conditions, qualifying payments and interactions without assuming multiple awards.

steps.title: Distinguish the people and payments
steps.outcome: Separate carer, cared-for person, Carer’s Allowance and a carer additional amount.
steps.practice: Draw a labelled people-and-payments diagram.

steps.title: Caring qualification
steps.outcome: Identify source-backed caring conditions separately from evidence that they are met.
steps.practice: Build a conditions-to-evidence checklist using only synthetic facts.

steps.title: Caring interactions
steps.outcome: Distinguish Carer’s Allowance from a Pension Credit carer addition and impacts on another person.
steps.practice: Draw directed claimant/carer/other-person effects and test an unsupported symmetry claim.

steps.title: Caring for several people
steps.outcome: Avoid inferring multiple payments from multiple caring responsibilities.
steps.practice: Compare one-person and two-person synthetic scenarios and justify every proposed change or non-conclusion.

steps.title: Evidence of caring
steps.outcome: Distinguish a condition from evidence that a synthetic case meets it.
steps.practice: Create an evidence checklist and identify unknown facts.

steps.title: Change the qualifying payment
steps.outcome: Re-evaluate dependencies when one relevant fact changes.
steps.practice: Record which conclusions must be withdrawn or rechecked.

steps.title: Caring assessment
steps.outcome: Give a supported scope statement and a safe next step.
steps.practice: Submit the directed map, source locators and unresolved evidence.

paths.title: Test whether OKF improves the AI demonstration
paths.description: Measure token use and evidence quality fairly without presuming the desired result.

steps.title: State a falsifiable hypothesis
steps.outcome: Separate token economy from answer quality.
steps.practice: Pre-register success thresholds and explicitly allow no improvement or worse results.

steps.title: Freeze the experiment
steps.outcome: Keep model, settings, question, source version and output budget comparable.
steps.practice: Create the input manifest and record unavoidable differences between conditions.

steps.title: Choose representative cases
steps.outcome: Cover ambiguity, dates, interactions and household qualification.
steps.practice: Select staff-002, 006, 008, 012, 026 and 033 plus an unknown-term control.

steps.title: Define the controls
steps.outcome: Distinguish raw-source versus OKF evidence from a no-evidence control.
steps.practice: Prepare equal-source A/B packages; retain no-evidence as a separate diagnostic, not the fair baseline.

steps.title: Measure all the costs
steps.outcome: Count prompts, tool returns, retries, output and amortised preparation separately.
steps.practice: Submit totals, latency and failure rates for repeated runs, with unavailable provider fields labelled.

steps.title: Review claims independently
steps.outcome: Separate citation match from correctness, qualifications and completeness.
steps.practice: Blind the treatment labels and score claims against the same frozen evidence.

steps.title: Replay and disclose
steps.outcome: Retain exact identities and explain failures or ties.
steps.practice: Replay the duplicate and unknown control; retain raw results and exclusions.

steps.title: Comparison assessment
steps.outcome: Make only conclusions supported by the experiment.
steps.practice: Submit a paired results table, variability, limitations and a reproducibility manifest.

paths.title: Design an accessible Pension Credit application journey
paths.description: Map an official form and its notes to a synthetic, accessible application flow without equating data collection with entitlement.

steps.title: Set the application boundary
steps.outcome: Separate a demonstration submission from an official claim.
steps.practice: Write the opening and confirmation copy; use fictional data and a local demo receipt.

steps.title: Acquire the form family
steps.outcome: Pin PC1, PC1 notes and PC1H as separate source artefacts.
steps.practice: Record publication version, original URLs, hashes, page locators and extraction checks.

steps.title: Trace each field
steps.outcome: Link collected data to an exact form question and purpose.
steps.practice: Build the form-question to field to validation to conditional-routing matrix.

steps.title: Represent uncertainty
steps.outcome: Keep unknown, empty, zero and not applicable distinct.
steps.practice: Create synthetic missing-data cases and explain what the user should do next.

steps.title: Model household branches
steps.outcome: Use validated form conditions to design household and care branches.
steps.practice: Trace two fictional journeys without deriving branches solely from benefit mention tags.

steps.title: Prototype with CASA
steps.outcome: Choose and pin a tested CASA package and accessible components.
steps.practice: Retain package identity, route tests, labels, error summary and keyboard results.

steps.title: Check answers and corrections
steps.outcome: Let a person inspect and change every answer before submission.
steps.practice: Demonstrate correction, cancellation and recovery with consistent state.

steps.title: Application-design assessment
steps.outcome: Prove field provenance and accessible completion.
steps.practice: Submit the field map, recordings and fictional receipt; block release if required source fields remain unverified.

paths.title: Demonstrate a trustworthy agent-assisted application
paths.description: Demonstrate callable browser tools that share validation and user control with the human application flow.

steps.title: Verify the host capability
steps.outcome: Distinguish tool registration from callable WebMCP in the actual host.
steps.practice: Record browser, host, API and one successful observed discovery/invocation; otherwise label the path blocked.

steps.title: Specify a small tool surface
steps.outcome: Define inspect, update, validate, review and submit operations with clear boundaries.
steps.practice: Write input/output contracts and state which operations mutate draft or submitted state.

steps.title: Share the validation
steps.outcome: Apply the same rules and state to human and tool-driven entry.
steps.practice: Submit the same invalid and valid values through both routes and compare outcomes.

steps.title: Keep the person in control
steps.outcome: Bind confirmation to the exact reviewed application state.
steps.practice: Show a changed answer invalidating earlier confirmation; do not treat conversation text as blanket submission authority.

steps.title: Test cancellation and retry
steps.outcome: Prevent duplicate submission and support recoverable tool failure.
steps.practice: Demonstrate a cancelled request, retry and one fictional receipt with a stable submission identity.

steps.title: Treat content as data
steps.outcome: Ignore instructions embedded in retrieved guidance or field content.
steps.practice: Run an inert injection fixture and show that it cannot alter permissions or submission policy.

steps.title: Measure parity and cost
steps.outcome: Compare the same completed application through human and agent routes.
steps.practice: Report correctness, recovery, calls, tokens and elapsed time without assuming the agent route wins.

steps.title: Agent-assistance assessment
steps.outcome: Prove callable capability, parity and informed confirmation.
steps.practice: Submit invocation evidence, a human-route comparison and failed-case logs; provide an honest non-WebMCP fallback if unavailable.

paths.title: From evidence to a reviewable rules prototype
paths.description: Separate evidence, propositions, reviewed rules and executable tests; block incomplete or unreviewed rules from award decisions.

steps.title: Challenge definitive-bundle assumptions
steps.outcome: Explain why a captured guide is not a complete executable legal specification.
steps.practice: Inventory temporal, statutory, exception and source gaps before defining a rule.

steps.title: Choose one bounded rule family
steps.outcome: State a small scope and exclude unsupported regimes.
steps.practice: Propose a Pension Credit input-validation or evidence-routing rule, not a full award calculator.

steps.title: Extract a proposition
steps.outcome: Retain conditions, negation, exceptions and source context.
steps.practice: Write one candidate proposition and link it to exact source passages.

steps.title: Record the interpretation
steps.outcome: Distinguish a source proposition from a model-proposed rule.
steps.practice: Produce a reviewer decision record with disagreements and unresolved points.

steps.title: Type inputs and outputs
steps.outcome: Represent dates, units and unknowns explicitly.
steps.practice: Create a typed decision table with indeterminate and out-of-scope outputs.

steps.title: Model dates and dependencies
steps.outcome: Bind rule variants to effective periods and complete support dependencies.
steps.practice: Show that removing an exception or applicable date blocks evaluation.

steps.title: Create synthetic boundary cases
steps.outcome: Test neighbouring values and changed material facts.
steps.practice: Submit positive, negative, missing-data, out-of-period and contradictory-evidence cases.

steps.title: Compare with independent review
steps.outcome: Avoid using the generating model as its own correctness oracle.
steps.practice: Have a designated reviewer check traceability and expected outcomes; keep specialist approval pending where unavailable.

steps.title: Design the promotion gate
steps.outcome: Prevent unreviewed rules becoming a public entitlement service.
steps.practice: Specify owner approval, legal validation, provenance, tests, rollback and monitoring before any operational use.

steps.title: Rules-capstone assessment
steps.outcome: Demonstrate a transparent non-operational prototype.
steps.practice: Submit the rule pack and a blocked case; no award, real claimant decision or claim of complete legal coverage.
